_doc: LEXICAL SUBSTITUTIONS, not respellings. Only for a word that is gone from modern Truku, where a different word now carries the meaning. Requires: (1) no reflex of his word anywhere in the omnibus by gloss, by fuzzy shape and by substring, and (2) his dictionary has no form of the modern word either. The app renders these as MODERN (his original), colour-coded, so the toggle never puts a word in his mouth. Keep this list short and evidenced.
_biri: Two entries, one token, and they want different answers -- so neither is given. BIRI 'Mouillé tout outre - trempé' is the modern bili 很濕 (truku_dict, 10x in speech, with psbili 被淋濕, spbili 使淋濕, kbili 成淋濕): a plain r/l respelling. BIRI 'Dernier' is a word that is gone -- biri is 0 everywhere, and 最後 is now khici / tqring / nhdan, a substitution. The map is keyed on the token and the search index is built from it, so one token cannot render two ways without breaking lookup. Null: both stay green, which is the honest colour for a reading that depends on which entry you are standing in.
_q'nao: Ail/garlic. Sweep of all 32,212 omnibus words found no qnaw-shaped Allium word; the whole modern field is qusul / pixil / neygi / sangas. He has no qusul-shaped word either, and he separates the native Q'NAO from the loan NEGI = oignon.
_sengse: Maitre - professeur. He tags it [emprunt jap./chin.] himself (sensei / 先生). sensi and sengse are absent from every corpus and are not in truku_dict. Modern Truku teaches with the native tgsa root: mtgsa 老師 (296 in speech), emptgsa 老師 (198), tmgsa (97), plus ttgsa 教材, ptgsa 使被教導, stgsa 為…教導. mtgsa is the commonest and is taken here.
_sl'xeq: Lecher / to lick / 舔. His SL'XEQ, which he himself only guesses at ("( = R. ? - R. = L'XEQ ?)"): he read the lick word as built on L'XEQ 皮/樹皮 = modern rhiq. It is not. srhiq, smrhiq and slhiq are absent from all three corpora (32,212-word omnibus, 33,145-entry truku_dict, 277k tokens of transcribed speech), and nothing glossed 舔 is shaped like them. The modern word is shik / smhik, glossed 吻 in the wordlists but translated 舔 wherever it is used of a tongue: 'Ga smhik baga na qnqan na emu ka laqi' 小孩子舔吃糖果的手, 'smhik ubal wawa na' 用舌舔毛, 'Pshpaha mu huling ka luqih' 讓狗舔我的傷口. Pecoraro has no shik-shaped form anywhere -- his word for a kiss is TONGOX -- so the two lexicons really don't share this word.
_sl'xqan: The derived slots of the same verb. shik has no locative, patient or imperative on record, so there is nothing to substitute and a null says so: frozen out of every tier, left green.
_stbako: Stbako 'to smell of tobacco' is his S- prefix on the same root, but slumak is unattested in all three corpora, so there is no modern form to name. Null: left green.
_tbako: Tobacco. His TBAKO is the Japanese loan, and it did not survive: tbaku, tbako, tmbaku and stbaku are absent from the omnibus, from truku_dict and from 277k tokens of speech. The modern word is the native lumak -- lumak 煙草（植物名）, pslumak 種植煙草, pnslumak 種過煙草, ptglumak 因煙草而死, rnabaw lumak 菸草 -- and his own idiom survives with it: he writes 'mqan tbako' (= manger du tabac) for smoking, and the omnibus says 'mkan lumak' 抽煙 over and over. He has no lumak-shaped word anywhere.
